title: My solo mobile RPG's first trailer: MiniMax H3 on local ComfyUI, ElevenLabs narration, and real gameplay. Plus how I keep sprite style consistent without a LoRA
author: chriskr7
selftext:
**Hero Returns** is a landscape mobile collection RPG I'm building solo in Unity, as a side project. Great historical figures (Yi Sun-sin, Mozart, Newton, Lincoln, Cao Cao...) fight with powers drawn from their achievements. You place 5 heroes on a 3x3 grid before each auto battle, and placement alone can flip a fight at equal power. Art style: 2-head-tall chibi, Korean ink-brush outlines, soft watercolor color.

Art was always the wall that stopped me as a solo dev, so here's the AI pipeline I ended up with:

**Sprites and animation**

- I forked the open-source [sprite-gen](https://github.com/aldegad/sprite-gen) and added a local ComfyUI provider, so everything runs on my own machine and goes straight into Unity.
- Style consistency without a LoRA: each hero starts from one approved base image. Every pose and animation frame is generated with that image as a reference plus a shared style prompt. Anything that drifts gets rerolled.

**The trailer (this video)**

- First frames: Z-Image Turbo
- Clips: MiniMax H3 on local ComfyUI (RTX 5090), using a turbo 4-step LoRA at 768p
- Narration: ElevenLabs
- Cut together with real gameplay footage in ffmpeg

Launching on Android and iOS in about a month. Pre-registration: https://heroreturns.app

Happy to go deeper on any part of the pipeline. How are you all keeping character style consistent across many sprites, base image references like this, or LoRAs?

comments.author: Shalke97
comments.body: Nice Trailer! Interesting game idea, did you come up with that yourself?

replies.author: chriskr7
replies.body: Thanks! Yes, it's a solo project, so the design is mine. I re-planned it from scratch about a month ago. The core idea is that each historical figure's powers come from what they actually achieved, and where you place them on the 3x3 grid matters as much as raw power. At equal power, placement alone can flip a fight.
